title: Reserve slicing & preemptable mix — sketch
content:
Purpose:
This is a working spreadsheet sketch and short rationale for a reserve-slicing offering: allow customers to break a large reserved GPU commit into smaller independently sized and timed 'slices', and optionally mix in a tranche of preemptable / spot-backed capacity to materially reduce blended unit costs while protecting a baseline of reserved throughput.

Context and motivation:
- Problem we keep seeing: customers commit to large monthly reserved pools to get predictable unit economics but then underutilize or have lumpy seasonal demand. This creates either wasted spend or conservative over-commit.
- Traditional approaches (single monolithic annual/monthly commit) force customers to pick one point on the utilization curve. We want a configurable middle ground: smaller slices + optional preemptable mix + phased activation windows.
- Goal: improve average utilization, reduce customer sticker price for the same effective sustained throughput, and keep our utilization high.

Key concepts (quick definitions):
- Slice: a sub-commit of N GPUs for a defined window (example: 10 GPUs for 90 days). Customers can hold multiple slices with overlapping windows.
- Baseline reserved capacity: the minimum guaranteed non-preemptable GPUs covered by reserve pricing.
- Preemptable tranche: separate pricing for preemptable GPUs (lower $/hr) with no SLA; customers can choose a % mix.
- Blended effective unit price: weighted average $/GPU-hour across baseline + preemptable + any overage pay-as-you-go.

Assumptions for modeling (cells referenced in the attached sheet tabs):
- Hourly costs to Redwood (infra amortized): non-preemptable GPU = $2.80 / GPU-hour; preemptable = $1.20 / GPU-hour.
- Market payg price we charge today baseline: $4.00 / GPU-hour non-preemptable payg.
- Target reserved discount: 35% vs payg (variable by term and commitment).
- Slice min size: 4 GPUs; max: matched to customer's peak.
- Typical customer profile simulated: steady baseline 20 GPUs 24/7 plus weekly burst to 50 GPUs for 4 hours per day.

Model structure (spreadsheet tabs and columns):
- tab: scenario_inputs (cells: baseline_demand_gpus, burst_gpus, burst_hours_per_day, calendar_days, preemptable_mix_pct, reserved_term_days, slice_size_gpus, slice_activation_schedule)
- tab: slice_costing (rows: slice_1..slice_n; cols: slice_size, term_days, price_per_gpu_hour_reserved, effective_discount, amortized_monthly_fee)
- tab: utilization_sim (minute/hour granularity; simulates demand and maps to baseline reserved, preemptable tranche, and payg overflow)
- tab: breakeven (simple analytic formulas for: threshold_utilization_pct where reserved becomes cheaper vs payg; breakeven_days for each slice)

Sample formulas (put these into the sheet):
- reserved_hourly_price = payg_hourly_price * (1 - target_discount)
- slice_total_hours = slice_size * term_days * 24
- slice_cost = slice_total_hours * reserved_hourly_price
- customer_effective_price_blended = (reserved_hours*reserved_price + preemptable_hours*preemptable_price + payg_overflow_hours*payg_price) / total_consumed_hours
- breakeven_util_pct = (reserved_price - preemptable_price) / (payg_price - preemptable_price) (approx for 2-tranche mix)

Numerical example (concrete scenario):
- Customer wants ~20 sustained GPUs. They agree to 16 GPUs reserved baseline in two slices of 8 GPUs for 90 days each (phased start), and choose 25% preemptable mix for burst coverage.
- Numbers: payg_price=4.00, reserved_discount=35% -> reserved_price=2.60, preemptable_price=1.20
- If utilization of reserved slice is 75% (i.e., 12/16 GPUs effectively used on average), blended unit price (rough calc):
  reserved_component = (12*2.60) / 12 = 2.60 (for those reserved hours)
  preemptable_component assume 4 GPUs * 24h * 30d * 1.20 -> lowers blended price when bursts use preemptable instead of payg
  blended roughly = ~2.20 / GPU-hour vs payg 4.00 (customer savings ~45%)
- For Redwood, blended margin remains positive because our internal costs baseline assumed $2.80 non-preemptable and $1.20 preemptable. Show amortized profitability in 'slice_costing' tab.

Tradeoffs & policies we need to define (policy cells / product rules):
- Slice cancellation: allow early cancellation with sliding credit schedule (e.g., credits proportional to unused days but apply 10% admin fee).
- Slice re-assignment: allow customers to shift activation windows between slices with 30 days notice; last-minute shifts allowed only if capacity available.
- Preemptable floor: ensure at least X% baseline non-preemptable is purchased for larger customers to protect SLA-sensitive workloads.
- Auto-fallback: when preemptable capacity not available, automatic fallback to payg at a negotiated capped rate to avoid customer outages (helps adoption).

Sensitivity testing to add (recommended sheet views):
- Vary reserved discount 25%/35%/45% and show delta to customer monthly bill for given utilization curves.
- Vary preemptable mix (0%/15%/30%/50%) and show Redwood blended margin and utilization.
- Vary slice granularity: 4/8/16 GPU slices and see administrative overhead vs utilization improvement.
- Probe churn scenarios: customers that underutilize in month 1 but ramp in month 2 – show 3-month rolling utilization and effective price.

Open questions & risks to validate with SRE/Infra finance: 
- Availability SLO for preemptable tranche and realistic preemptable uplift factor in real fleet (is our preemptable supply reliably available for 6 months windows?).
- Accounting treatment: how to amortize committed revenue for slices spanning multiple fiscal periods. Finance needs the amortization schedule template (sheet: acct_amort).
- Edge-case pricing: how to price for extremely bursty but infrequent usage (e.g., 2 hours/day bursts but 10x magnitude). Does a slice still make sense vs pure payg?
- Operational complexity: inventorying many small slices increases orchestration and billing complexity; need an SLO for ops cost per slice.

Proposed next steps (owners + timeline rough):
- Engineering (Marco): add hourly simulation harness to 'utilization_sim' tab and wire to our historical telemetry to validate model (2 weeks).
- Finance (Dana): validate infra cost assumptions and produce amortization template (acct_amort tab) (1 week).
- Solutions / Sales (Sanjay): draft go-to-market positioning and sample customer pitch with ROI charts (1 week).
- Product (Aisha): run sensitivity sweeps and produce 3 canonical offers (conservative, balanced, aggressive) and recommended default (2 weeks).

Decision criteria for launch:
- 3 canonical offers yield >20% customer bill savings in 2/3 representative customer profiles AND Redwood blended margin >= current baseline margin.
- SRE signs off on sustainable preemptable supply assumptions for 6+ month windows.
- Billing and accounting can support slice-level invoicing without > 15% increased ops cost (modeled).

Notes / scratch items (informal):
- Consider an API-first billing model so slices can be programmatically created/terminated and monitored.
- Potential upsell: predictive autoslice — system adds short slices automatically ahead of predicted bursts (requires workload forecasting).
- Early adopter promotion: waive first-slice admin fee for first 3 customers to get data.

Attachments (sheet tabs we will create):
- scenario_inputs, slice_costing, utilization_sim, breakeven, acct_amort, sensitivity_summary, example_customer_presentation

This is a working sketch — many cells will be placeholder formulas. Please clone the sheet and add real telemetry-backed hourly demand traces in utilization_sim for the customers you care about.

END OF SKETCH
